title: Client invoices and follow-ups

agent.name: Lakshmi
agent.instructions: Keep messages to clients polite and short.

memories.content: Client Neha is often late; ask for 50% advance
Invoices in rupees; GSTIN not registered yet

topics.ask: Ravi owes me ₹45,000 for the dashboard design, invoice sent on 2026-09-28. Neha owes ₹30,000 since 2026-08-30. Draft follow-ups.
topics.answer: To Ravi (polite reminder): Hi Ravi, a quick reminder that the invoice for the dashboard design (₹45,000, sent on 28 September) is due. Could you let me know when the payment is planned? Thanks! To Neha (firmer, overdue since 30 August): Hi Neha, the invoice of ₹30,000 from 30 August is now overdue by more than six weeks. Could you please clear it this week, or tell me a date by which you can? For the next project I'll need a 50% advance before starting. Thanks for understanding.

topics.ask: Neha replied she'll pay ₹15,000 now and the rest at month end. OK?
topics.answer: That's reasonable if you get it in writing. Reply: Thanks Neha, ₹15,000 now and the remaining ₹15,000 by 31 October works. Please confirm. Then record both dates in your tracker and I'll remind you on 1 November to check the second payment. Keep the 50% advance rule for her next project.

topics.ask: Make a simple tracker for all my invoices.
topics.answer: Columns: invoice number, client, project, amount, date sent, due date, amount received, date received, status (sent, partly paid, paid, overdue) and next action. Today it has Ravi ₹45,000 sent 28 September and due 13 October, and Neha ₹30,000 sent 30 August, ₹15,000 promised now and ₹15,000 by 31 October. Review it every Monday.

ask: What's outstanding right now and what should I send today?
